author: claude
headline: Liverpool cranes likely stopped on Tuesday as Atlantic storms slow arrivals

summary.ports: Liverpool likely stops cranes Tue 10:00–22:00; gusty spells at six other ports; London Gateway clear
summary.weather: US East Coast and Canada services 2 days or more late; Asia via the Cape 1–2 days
summary.news: Hapag-Lloyd suspends bookings to three Philippine ports; MSC restores Karachi to Europe

port_notes.felixstowe: Gusty Mon 20:00–21:00 only: release and deliver as planned
port_notes.southampton: Gusty Mon and Tue mornings: avoid tight morning cut-offs
port_notes.london_gateway: Clear all week: book release and delivery now
port_notes.liverpool: Cranes likely stopped Tue 10:00–22:00: move collections to Wed, allow 24–48 hours
port_notes.rotterdam: Gusty Tue 16:00–18:00: allow 12–24 hours on feeder connections
port_notes.antwerp: Gusty Tue afternoon and from Fri evening: allow 12–24 hours
port_notes.bremerhaven: Gusty Tue night to Wed 10:00: allow 12–24 hours on Wed calls
port_notes.hamburg: Gusty Tue 12:00–15:00 and Tue night: keep Wed morning flexible

inbound_note: Confirm revised ETAs for anything coming from North America or round the Cape before you book haulage.

sections.advisories: Hapag-Lloyd has stopped taking bookings to three Philippine ports, and MSC has restored a direct Karachi service to seven European ports. Surcharges keep rising on US inland haulage and West Africa.
sections.reliability: In August, Sea-Intelligence counted 49.9% of ships on time and Xeneta 29%. Plan on about half of arrivals missing their scheduled day.
